resolves_review.finding_title: A denied claim is reintroduced through a second actor public claim

review_conclusions: The selector validates participating canonical context packs and their dossier binding before reading projected source-bound claims; missing packs cannot downgrade into raw dossier reads.

Literal False at either top-level or qualifier position wins over public visibility and conflicting literal True. Denied identities are accumulated across all validated participating actors/dimensions before the final global filter, making row/actor order irrelevant under the existing shared-claim identity.
The implementation never mutates canonical packs; permanent duplicate tests revalidate persisted seals, retain modeler audit and preserve other-actor authorized knowledge.
The original independent two-actor reproducer now passes in both actor orders; the permanent 16-case suite passes independently.
The exact baseline-selector comparison demonstrates 12 expected failures and 4 positive passes, then 16 current passes; all six channels show zero denied exposure in the current version.
No blocking correctness finding remains within the exact normalized-claim shared-context slice.
review_harness_correction: The first final independent run passed all 16 permanent cases but its two older external cases assumed world-brief injection always creates _system_message. Correct denial filtering can make the brief empty, preserving the original message; the harness then raised AttributeError before observing channels. A separate corrected reproducer reads effective message or original fallback. The corrected 18-case run passes; the failed receipt and original reproducer/evidence are preserved. No runtime edit was needed.
remaining_scope: This approval covers source-bound canonical shared claim selection and its six offline consumers, not full app acceptance.
Semantic paraphrase matching, per-recipient public feeds, broader ontology/report integration and production provider behavior are not proven by this change.
Global suppression is a conservative tradeoff for a universally shared brief; authorized actor-local knowledge remains available.
No original checkout, runtime/saved-run artifacts or repository code/tests/docs were modified by the reviewer.
